readings.title: The First Plague: Blood
readings.subtitle: The Waters of the Nile Turned
readings.text: [Exodus 7:14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“The heart of Pharaoh is hard, he refuses to let <dn>את</dn> the people go.</dq> [15] <dq>“Go to Pharaoh in the morning, as he goes out to the water, and you shall stand by the river’s bank to meet him. And take in your hand <dn>את</dn> the rod which was turned into a serpent.</dq> [16] <dq>“And you shall say to him, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of the Hebrews has sent me to you, saying, “Let <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people go, so that they serve <dn>Me</dn> in the wilderness.” But see, until now you have not listened!</dq> [17] <dq>‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “By this you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. See, <dn>I</dn> am striking <dn>את</dn> the waters which are in the river with the rod that is in my hand, and they shall be turned to blood.</dq> [18] <dq>“And the fish in the river shall die, and the river shall stink, and the Mitsrites shall find it impossible to drink <dn>את</dn> the water of the river.” ’ ”</dq> [19] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Say to Aharon, ‘Take <dn>את</dn> your rod and stretch out <dn>את</dn> your hand over the waters of Mitsrayim, over their streams, over their rivers, and over their ponds, and over all their pools of water, that they become blood. And there shall be blood in all the land of Mitsrayim, both in wooden and in stone containers.’ ”</dq> [20] And Mosheh and Aharon did so, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded. And he lifted up the rod and struck <dn>את</dn> the waters that were in the river, in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants. And all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood. [21] And the fish in the river died, and the river stank, and the Mitsrites were unable to drink <dn>את</dn> the water of the river. And the blood was in all the land of Mitsrayim. [22] And the magicians of Mitsrayim did the same with their magic. And the heart of Pharaoh was strengthened, and he did not listen to them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said. [23] And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and his heart was not moved by this either. [24] And all the Mitsrites dug around the river for water to drink, for they were unable to drink of the water of the river.

readings.title: The Second Plague: Frogs
readings.subtitle: A Land Covered in Creatures
readings.text: [Exodus 7:25] And seven days were completed after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had struck <dn>את</dn> the river. [Exodus 8:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, <dq>“Go to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Let <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people go, so that they serve <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [2] <dq>“And if you refuse to let them go, see, <dn>I</dn> am smiting <dn>את</dn> all your borders with frogs.</dq> [3] <dq>“And the river shall swarm with frogs, which shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedroom, and on your bed, and into the houses of your servants, and on your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneading bowls.</dq> [4] <dq>“And the frogs shall come up on you and on your people and on all your servants.” ’ ”</dq> [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Say to Aharon, ‘Stretch out <dn>את</dn> your hand with your rod over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause <dn>את</dn> frogs to come up on the land of Mitsrayim.’ ”</dq> [6] So Aharon stretched out <dn>את</dn> his hand over the waters of Mitsrayim, and the frogs came up and covered <dn>את</dn> the land of Mitsrayim. [7] And the magicians did the same with their magic, and brought up <dn>את</dn> frogs on the land of Mitsrayim. [8] Then Pharaoh called for Mosheh and Aharon, and said, “Pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to take away the frogs from me and from my people, and I shall let <dn>את</dn> the people go to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [9] And Mosheh said to Pharaoh, “Explain yourself to me: when shall I pray for you, and for your servants, and for your people, to destroy the frogs from you and your houses, and remain only in the river?” [10] And he said, “Tomorrow.” And he said, “Let it be according to your word, so that you know that there is no one like <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>. [11] “And the frogs shall depart from you, and from your houses, and from your servants, and from your people. They shall remain in the river only.” [12] And Mosheh and Aharon went out from Pharaoh. And Mosheh cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the frogs which <dn>He</dn> had brought against Pharaoh. [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did according to the word of Mosheh. And the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courtyards, and out of the fields. [14] And they gathered <dn>את</dn> them together in heaps, and the land stank. [15] And when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened <dn>את</dn> his heart and did not listen to them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said.

readings.title: The Third Plague: Gnats
readings.subtitle: The Finger of Elohim
readings.text: [Exodus 8:16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Say to Aharon, ‘Stretch out <dn>את</dn> your rod, and strike <dn>את</dn> the dust of the land, so that it becomes gnats in all the land of Mitsrayim.’ ”</dq> [17] And they did so. And Aharon stretched out <dn>את</dn> his hand with his rod and struck <dn>את</dn> the dust of the land, and it became gnats on man and beast. All the dust of the land became gnats in all the land of Mitsrayim. [18] And the magicians did the same with their magic to bring forth <dn>את</dn> gnats, but they were unable. So there were gnats on man and beast. [19] Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of <dn>Elohim</dn>.” But Pharaoh’s heart was strengthened, and he did not listen to them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said.

readings.title: The Fourth Plague: Flies
readings.subtitle: A Distinction for Goshen
readings.text: [Exodus 8:20] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh as he comes out to the water. And you shall say to him, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Let <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people go, so that they serve <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [21] <dq>“For if you do not let <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people go, see, <dn>I</dn> am sending <dn>את</dn> swarms of flies on you and your servants, and on your people and into your houses. And the houses of the Mitsrites shall be filled with swarms of flies, and also the ground on which they stand.</dq> [22] <dq>“And in that day <dn>I</dn> shall separate <dn>את</dn> the land of Goshen, in which <dn>My</dn> people are dwelling, that no swarms of flies shall be there, so that you know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the midst of the land.</dq> [23] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall put a distinction between <dn>My</dn> people and your people. Tomorrow this sign shall be.” ’ ”</dq> [24] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did so. And thick swarms of flies came into the house of Pharaoh, and into his servants’ houses, and into all the land of Mitsrayim. The land was laid waste because of the swarms of flies. [25] Then Pharaoh called for Mosheh and Aharon, and said, “Go, slaughter to your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the land.” [26] And Mosheh said, “It is not right to do so, for we would be slaughtering <dn>את</dn> the abomination of the Mitsrites to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>. If we slaughter <dn>את</dn> the abomination of the Mitsrites before their eyes, would they not stone us? [27] “Let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness and slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> as <dn>He</dn> shall command us.” [28] And Pharaoh said, “I let <dn>את</dn> you go, then you shall slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the wilderness. Only, do not go very far away. Pray for me.” [29] And Mosheh said, “See, I am going out from you, and I shall pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the swarms of flies shall depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, tomorrow. Only, let not Pharaoh again deceive by not letting <dn>את</dn> the people go to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [30] And Mosheh went out from Pharaoh and prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [31] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did according to the word of Mosheh. And <dn>He</dn> removed <dn>את</dn> the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. Not one remained. [32] But Pharaoh hardened <dn>את</dn> his heart at this time also, and he did not let <dn>את</dn> the people go.

readings.title: The Fifth Plague: Livestock
readings.subtitle: Death in the Fields
readings.text: [Exodus 9:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Go in to Pharaoh and speak to him, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of the Hebrews, “Let <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people go, so that they serve <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [2] <dq>“For if you refuse to let them go, and still hold them,</dq> [3] <dq>“see, the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is on your livestock in the field, on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the cattle, and on the sheep – a very grievous pestilence.</dq> [4] <dq>“And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall separate between the livestock of Yisra’el and the livestock of Mitsrayim, and let nothing die of all that belongs to the children of Yisra’el.” ’ ”</dq> [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> set a chosen time, saying, <dq>“Tomorrow <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall do this word in the land.”</dq> [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did <dn>את</dn> this word on the next day, and all the livestock of Mitsrayim died. But of the livestock of the children of Yisra’el, not one died. [7] And Pharaoh sent, and see, not even one of the livestock of Yisra’el was dead. But the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not let <dn>את</dn> the people go.

readings.title: The Sixth Plague: Boils
readings.subtitle: Unclean and Afflicted
readings.text: [Exodus 9:8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh and Aharon, <dq>“Take for yourselves handfuls of ashes from a furnace, and let Mosheh scatter it toward the heavens in the eyes of Pharaoh.</dq> [9] <dq>“And it shall become fine dust in all the land of Mitsrayim, and it shall cause boils that break out in sores on man and beast in all the land of Mitsrayim.”</dq> [10] So they took <dn>את</dn> ashes from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh, and Mosheh scattered it toward the heavens. And it caused boils breaking out in sores on man and beast. [11] And the magicians were unable to stand before Mosheh because of the boils, for the boils were on the magicians and on all the Mitsrites. [12] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> strengthened <dn>את</dn> the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not listen to them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said to Mosheh.

readings.title: The Seventh Plague: Hail
readings.subtitle: Thunder and Fire Upon the Earth
readings.text: [Exodus 9:13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and say to him, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of the Hebrews, “Let <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people go, so that they serve <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [14] <dq>“for at this time <dn>I</dn> am sending <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> plagues unto your heart, and on your servants and on your people, so that you know that there is no one like <dn>Me</dn> in all the earth.</dq> [15] <dq>“Now if <dn>I</dn> had stretched out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand and struck <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> your people with pestilence, then you would have been cut off from the earth.</dq> [16] <dq>“And for this cause <dn>I</dn> have raised you up, in order to show you <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> power, and in order to declare <dn>My</dn> Name in all the earth.</dq> [17] <dq>“You still exalt yourself against <dn>My</dn> people by not letting them go.</dq> [18] <dq>“See, tomorrow about this time <dn>I</dn> am causing very heavy hail to rain down, such as has not been in Mitsrayim from the day of its founding until now.</dq> [19] <dq>“And now, send, bring <dn>את</dn> your livestock to safety and <dn>את</dn> all that you have in the field, for every man and beast that is found in the field and is not brought home, the hail shall come down on them and they shall die.” ’ ”</dq> [20] He who feared <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> among the servants of Pharaoh made <dn>את</dn> his servants and <dn>את</dn> livestock flee to the houses. [21] But he who did not set <dn>את</dn> his heart on the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> left <dn>את</dn> his servants and <dn>את</dn> his livestock in the field. [22] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Stretch out <dn>את</dn> your hand toward the heavens, and let there be hail in all the land of Mitsrayim, on man, and on beast, and on every herb of the field, throughout the land of Mitsrayim.”</dq> [23] And Mosheh stretched out <dn>את</dn> his rod toward the heavens. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent thunder and hail, and fire came down to the earth. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rained hail on the land of Mitsrayim. [24] And there was hail, and fire flashing among the hail, very heavy, such as had not been in all the land of Mitsrayim since it became a nation. [25] And the hail struck in all the land of Mitsrayim <dn>את</dn> all that was in the field, both man and beast. And the hail struck <dn>את</dn> every herb of the field and broke <dn>את</dn> every tree of the field. [26] Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Yisra’el were, there was no hail. [27] And Pharaoh sent and called for Mosheh and Aharon, and said to them, “I have sinned this time. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is righteous, and I and my people are wrong. [28] “Pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for there has been enough of the thunder and hail of <dn>Elohim</dn>. and I let <dn>את</dn> you go, and you stay no longer.” [29] And Mosheh said to him, <dq>“As soon as I go out of the city, I stretch out <dn>את</dn> my hands to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the thunder ceases and there is no more hail, so that you know that the earth belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [30] <dq>“But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn>.”</dq> [31] And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in the head and the flax was in bud. [32] But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they are late crops. [33] And Mosheh went out of the city from Pharaoh and stretched out his hands to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the thunder and the hail ceased, and the rain was not poured on the earth. [34] And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder had ceased, he sinned yet more and hardened <dn>את</dn> his heart, he and his servants. [35] And the heart of Pharaoh was strengthened, and he did not let <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’el go, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said through Mosheh.
